topic: The 2.4x gap between in-model (~236 us/layer) and isolated (~98 us/layer) cost of the same Q4 decode GEMV kernels: between-dispatch state candidates tested one at a time in isolation
decision: RECEIPT-ONLY. The 138 us/layer gap is not a between-dispatch state problem and not recoverable decode time. It is an instrument mismatch: the isolated 98 us/layer was summed from per-dispatch honeykrisp device-timestamp intervals, whose absolute scale is not trustworthy (documented in receipts/2026-09-10-dispatch-floor and receipts/2026-09-10-q4-gemv-bandwidth; re-demonstrated inside this run). Wall-clock-anchored, the SAME four dispatches cost 203 us/layer isolated and the in-model interleaved analog costs 207 us/layer - interleaving costs +1.8%, and the residual difference from the 236 us/layer production number is the lm_head dispatch amortized into the per-layer figure. No source change is supported; the six canonical digests were not exercised (nothing landed).
host: jwm1-linux (100.84.184.102), Apple M1 (G13G B1), Honeykrisp installed package mesa-honeykrisp-omarchy 26.3.0.devel.hk6f6afc8-1, linux-asahi 7.1.6, glslc 2026.3

method: New --gap mode in tools/q4-bw-bench reproduces the in-model decode interleaving in isolation and moves ONE factor at a time: 24 independent per-layer weight sets (8,427,008 bytes/layer x 24 = 202 MB, the exact four Qwen2.5-0.5B decode dispatch shapes through the production shader), RAW-chained or independent descriptor variants, a peak_read streaming filler between GEMV dispatches, fresh-allocation churn, and two-submission splits.

iso4_isolated_calibration.note: one weight set, four dispatches, no chaining - the honest isolated cost

fill2_interstitial_2MB.note: +47 us is the filler's own streaming work; GEMV time unchanged - no eviction penalty

fill24_forced_24MB.note: filler dominates by design; GEMV portion unchanged

sweep_residency.reading: FLAT from an 8.4 MB cache-fitting footprint to the full 202 MB token working set - the kernels get zero benefit from weight residency at any cache level

instrument_artifact_two_independent_meas.measurement_1_wall_vs_timestamp_same_ker: wall-anchored isolated iso4 = 202.9 us/layer (median of both runs, pass 2) vs the timestamp-based 98.0 us/layer sum (bench-a, receipts/2026-09-10-q4-gemv-native-map) for the SAME four dispatches, SAME shader body, SAME machine, SAME defines: the device-timestamp instrument undercounted by 2.07x
instrument_artifact_two_independent_meas.measurement_2_physical_impossibility: the old number implies 86.0 GB/s of weight streaming against a 68.25 GB/s DRAM part - impossible for a workload that reads 202 MB of weights per token from memory; the wall-anchored rate is 41.5 GB/s
instrument_artifact_two_independent_meas.supporting: this same run's timestamp-based peak probe reports a 512 MB copy in 41,833 device ns = 12.8 TB/s - the documented device-clock nonsense, re-demonstrated on the same boot as the gap arms

composition_artifact.what: the in-model 236 us/layer (b6d662a ablation marginal 5.68 ms/token over 97 dispatches) includes the lm_head GEMV (151,936x896 q4 = 72.3 MB, one dispatch) amortized over 24 layers
composition_artifact.correction: at 55-70 GB/s for its 18,992-workgroup grid, lm_head costs ~1.0-1.3 ms/token, so the true per-layer projection cost in-model is ~180-195 us/layer - equal to or FASTER than the wall-anchored isolated 203 us/layer within instrument bound
composition_artifact.conclusion: in-model interleaving imposes no measurable penalty on the GEMV dispatches

prior_receipt_corrections_for_policy_own: receipts/2026-09-10-q4-gemv-bandwidth: 'achieved 1.1-1.20 GB/s' divided one layer's traffic (9.36 MB) by a full token of GPU time; per-token q4 weight traffic is ~202 MB + 72 MB lm_head, giving ~48 GB/s in-model - and its 'bench_isolated_kernel_ticks' absolute values rest on the same untrustworthy device clock as everything else

the 'warm 9.3 MB working set (SLC-resident)' interpretation of isolated results is superseded by this run's sweep: residency produces NO measurable effect (flat 203-209 us/layer from 1 to 24 sets), so SLC residency explains neither the old isolated numbers (clock artifacts do) nor anything else
receipts/2026-09-10-decode-attribution-finish microbench row 'gemv_layer 72.7 us/disp' is the eager harness floor, not a kernel number; its ablation marginals remain valid (wall-anchored)

why_no_landing: The evidence supports no digest-preserving source change: in-model dispatch cost is at parity with isolated (isolated is if anything the slower side), the kernel chain runs at its intrinsic ~41.5 GB/s (61% of the 68.25 GB/s part) in EVERY context, and the only real between-dispatch term (submission boundary, <= 0.33 ms/token upper bound) is within reach of no small change - closing it requires merging mlx-lm's two per-token graph evals or adding speculative commit deferral, both behavior-risky for a bound, not a measured in-model win. Per the assignment's own bar: receipt-only. Digest legs not exercised (nothing landed). The remaining kernel headroom (203 us/layer vs the 123 us/layer full-DRAM-peak floor) is inside the kernel and already shown unreachable by bit-pinned candidates in receipts/2026-09-10-q4-gemv-bandwidth and receipts/2026-09-10-q4-gemv-native-map.
